previous.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

previous.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
previous.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
previous.idiomatic: Fearing that events might change, the empress submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince be reduced to commoner status; the emperor approved by edict.

unit.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
unit.literal: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Rong, Prince of Liang, Eastern Garrison General Yun, Prince of Huainan, Forward General Eastern Martial Duke Dan, Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Grand Guardian He Shao to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as commoner.
unit.idiomatic: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Eastern Martial Duke; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the Crown Prince as a commoner.

next.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
next.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
next.idiomatic: Yu took the edict from the garden and rode an ox-cart out.

previous.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
previous.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.
previous.idiomatic: The crown prince had been deposed for no fault of his own, and people were indignant.

unit.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
unit.literal: Sima Ya, a commandant of the Right Guard and a distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, both enjoyed the crown prince's favor. Deeply grieved, they spoke to Sun Xiu, an adviser to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no rightful heir, the altars of soil and grain will be endangered, and disaster will surely arise for the great ministers.
unit.idiomatic: Sima Ya, a Right Guard commandant and distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, were both favored by the crown prince. Deeply grieved, they told Sun Xiu, an adviser to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no rightful heir; the dynasty is in danger, and disaster will surely come upon the great ministers.

next.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
next.literal: You serve the inner palace and are close to Empress Jia; everyone says you knew of the crown prince's deposition beforehand. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you.

context.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
context.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
context.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess, and the crown prince likewise wanted to marry into the Han family to strengthen his own position.

context.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
context.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
context.idiomatic: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused; instead, they betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

context.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
context.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.
context.idiomatic: The empress accepted what he said and spread accounts of the crown prince's faults far and wide.

context.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
context.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.
context.idiomatic: People at court and throughout the country knew that Empress Jia intended to harm the crown prince.

context.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
context.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year a mulberry sprouted west of the palace, growing over a chi daily for days before withering.
context.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the western wing of the palace, grew more than a chi each day, and withered after several days.

context.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
context.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
context.idiomatic: When he arrived, the empress did not see him but put him in a separate room. She sent the maid Chen Wu with wine and jujubes and pressed him to drink until he was drunk.

context.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
context.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.
context.idiomatic: The crown prince, too drunk and confused to understand, copied it as directed, but half the characters were malformed.

context.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
context.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.
context.idiomatic: Afterward the incomplete characters were filled in, and the empress showed the text to the emperor.

context.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
context.literal: It was shown to all the princes and officials; none spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who spoke in the crown prince's defense.
context.idiomatic: It was shown to all the princes and officials; none spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who spoke in the crown prince's defense.

context.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
context.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.
context.idiomatic: Fearing that events might change, the empress submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince be reduced to commoner status; the emperor approved by edict.

context.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
context.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.
context.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate attendant confess that he intended to rebel with the crown prince.

context.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
context.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.
context.idiomatic: An edict circulated the attendant's confession among the dukes and ministers.

context.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
context.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.
context.idiomatic: Earlier, when the crown prince was deposed, his consort's father Wang Yan submitted a memorial requesting a divorce.

context.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
context.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.
context.idiomatic: The crown prince had been deposed for no fault of his own, and people were indignant.

context.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
context.literal: Sima Ya, a commandant of the Right Guard and a distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, both enjoyed the crown prince's favor. Deeply grieved, they spoke to Sun Xiu, an adviser to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no rightful heir, the altars of soil and grain will be endangered, and disaster will surely arise for the great ministers.
context.idiomatic: Sima Ya, a Right Guard commandant and distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, were both favored by the crown prince. Deeply grieved, they told Sun Xiu, an adviser to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no rightful heir; the dynasty is in danger, and disaster will surely come upon the great ministers.

context.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
context.literal: You serve the inner palace and are close to Empress Jia; everyone says you knew of the crown prince's deposition beforehand. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you.
context.idiomatic: You serve the inner palace and are close to Empress Jia; everyone says you knew of the crown prince's deposition beforehand. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you.

context.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
context.literal: Xiu told Lun, Prince of Zhao, who readily accepted the proposal.
context.idiomatic: Sun Xiu told Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, who readily accepted the proposal.

context.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
context.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.
context.idiomatic: You have long served Empress Jia, and people in the streets all call you a partisan of the Jia family.

context.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
context.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.
context.idiomatic: Even if you now seek to do the crown prince a great service, though he might suppress his old resentment, he surely cannot reward you. He will think you changed sides under pressure from the people's expectations only to escape punishment.

context.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
context.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.
context.idiomatic: If any fault should come to light, you would still not escape execution.

context.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
context.literal: Better to delay and postpone the appointed time. Empress Jia will surely harm the crown prince; then depose her and avenge him. That alone will be enough to count as a merit, and only then can you achieve your aim.'
context.idiomatic: Better to delay and postpone the appointed time. Empress Jia will surely harm the crown prince; then depose her and avenge him. That alone will be enough to count as a merit, and only then can you achieve your aim."

context.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
context.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.
context.idiomatic: Xiu then used counter-agents to spread word that people inside the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome back the crown prince.

context.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
context.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
context.idiomatic: Lü told Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince into a small compound and gave him no food at all; nevertheless, people in the palace passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

context.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
context.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.
context.idiomatic: Lü then pressed the medicine on the crown prince, who refused to take it. When the crown prince went to the privy, Lü struck him dead with a medicine pestle. The crown prince cried out loudly, and his voice was heard outside.

context.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
context.literal: Although Yu's guilt could scarcely be greater, he is still a descendant of the sovereign. To send him to burial as an ordinary commoner truly moves me to pity. I especially beg Your Majesty's grace to grant him the rites of a prince.
context.idiomatic: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.

context.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
context.literal: In obedience to his final command, I established you as heir apparent, to bring glory to our ancestors.
context.idiomatic: In obedience to his final command, I established you as heir apparent, to bring glory to our ancestors.

context.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
context.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.
context.idiomatic: But I was blind to the vicious plotting, so that you suffered the calamity of an unnatural death: Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji have appeared again in our own day.

context.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
context.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.
context.idiomatic: Thanks to the wisdom of my ministers, and to the indignation of people and spirits, my mind was opened. I punished those responsible, and all received the penalty for their crimes.

context.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
context.literal: But how can this lessen the cruel suffering of your unjustly afflicted spirit?
context.idiomatic: But how can this lessen the cruel suffering of your unjustly afflicted spirit?

context.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
context.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.
context.idiomatic: Thus grief and regret shake me to my innermost being.

context.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
context.literal: When the funeral procession set out, a great wind arose with thunder and lightning, and its curtains and canopies were blown apart.
context.idiomatic: When the funeral procession set out, a great wind arose with thunder and lightning, and its curtains and canopies were blown apart.

context.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
context.literal: From childhood you were endowed with outstanding gifts; your fragrant virtue grew luxuriant.
context.idiomatic: From childhood you were endowed with outstanding gifts; your fragrant virtue grew luxuriant.

context.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
context.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
context.idiomatic: Long ago your sage ancestor prized your goodness and fine qualities.

context.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
context.literal: Therefore you were established as heir, to continue the imperial foundation forever.
context.idiomatic: Therefore you were established as heir, to continue the imperial foundation forever.

context.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
context.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
context.idiomatic: How could the cruel and violent secretly plot, bringing calamity like this?

context.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
context.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
context.idiomatic: Sorrow moves the harmonious breath of nature; anguish reaches through the four seasons.

context.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
context.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!
context.idiomatic: Alas, how sorrowful!

context.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
context.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.
context.idiomatic: That you were degraded and deposed was truly due to my blindness.

context.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
context.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!
context.idiomatic: Among all those who possess understanding, who is not stricken with grief?

context.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
context.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.
context.idiomatic: Though the ages differ, the pattern is the same; past and present follow one principle.

context.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
context.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.
context.idiomatic: The burial chamber has now been prepared, and your spirit will be laid to rest.

context.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
context.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.
context.idiomatic: A vast array of feathered canopies; rank upon rank of officials.

context.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
context.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!
context.idiomatic: All share the same grief and pain: who does not feel bitter sorrow?

context.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
context.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.
context.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Minhuai.

context.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
context.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.
context.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the sixth month, he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

context.zh: 臧字敬文。
context.literal: Zang, courtesy name Jingwen.
context.idiomatic: Zang's courtesy name was Jingwen.

context.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。
context.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.
context.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongkang's first year, he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.

context.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。
context.literal: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.
context.idiomatic: Now I establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.

context.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
context.literal: The crown prince's officials shall immediately become officials of the imperial grandson-heir.
context.idiomatic: The crown prince's officials shall immediately become officials of the imperial grandson-heir.

context.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
context.literal: Lun, Prince of Zhao, shall act as Grand Mentor to the imperial grandson-heir.'
context.idiomatic: Lun, Prince of Zhao, shall act as Grand Mentor to the imperial grandson-heir."

context.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。
context.literal: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.
context.idiomatic: When they reached Bronze Camel Street, the palace attendants wept, the attendants all sobbed, and passersby wiped away their tears.

context.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
context.literal: The mulberry tree grew again in the western wing; when the imperial grandson was deposed, it withered.
context.idiomatic: The mulberry tree grew again in the western wing; when the imperial grandson was deposed, it withered.

context.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
context.literal: In the first month of Yongning's first year, Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne. He reduced the grandson to Prince of Puyang; the grandson and the emperor were both moved to Jinyong, and the grandson was killed soon afterward.
context.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongning's first year, Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne. He reduced the grandson to Prince of Puyang; the grandson and the emperor were both moved to Jinyong, and the grandson was killed soon afterward.

context.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。
context.literal: Early in Tai'an posthumous title Ai was granted.
context.idiomatic: Early in Tai'an he was posthumously given the name Ai.

context.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
context.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
context.idiomatic: The historian says: Minhuai showed a remarkably intelligent bearing and a precociously mature nature.

context.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
context.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
context.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned their hearts toward him and had considerable hopes for his future.

context.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
context.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.
context.idiomatic: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover what was hidden, and none of the many officials showed the integrity of a remonstrating minister.

context.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
context.literal: Although the rites of mourning and honor were complete and the grief and pity profound, how could they help the one who had suffered such cruelty?
context.idiomatic: Although the rites of mourning and honor were complete and the grief and pity profound, how could they help the one who had suffered such cruelty?

context.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
context.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
context.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

context.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
context.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
context.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather treasured him; the assembled officials craned their necks in expectation.

context.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
context.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.
context.idiomatic: Once he fell victim to ruthless cruelty, hope for his return was in vain.

context.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
context.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.
context.idiomatic: At the time observers of portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven, so he was enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, with a fief of fifty thousand households.

context.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
context.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
context.idiomatic: The court made an extensive selection of men of virtue and standing as his tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

context.zh: 永康元年四月，封為襄陽王。
context.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang.
context.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongkang's first year, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiangyang.

context.zh: 永寧元年八月，立為皇太孫。
context.literal: In the eighth month of Yongning year one he was established as imperial grandson-heir.
context.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongning's first year, he was established as imperial grandson-heir.

context.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
context.literal: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Rong, Prince of Liang, Eastern Garrison General Yun, Prince of Huainan, Forward General Eastern Martial Duke Dan, Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Grand Guardian He Shao to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as commoner.
context.idiomatic: Thereupon Minister Director He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Eastern Martial Duke; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the Crown Prince as a commoner.
